performance.appWide: Hive-wide, not this workspace’s: {inFlight, plural, one {# request} other {# requests}} in flight · {refused, number} refused before Hive knew whose · event streams: {connections, plural, one {# connection} other {# connections}}, {events, number} events, {size}.
performance.card.dataTip: Bodies only, in UTF-8 bytes: what Hive's API sent and received. Not provider traffic: Hive isn't between the CLIs and their providers.
performance.card.guidanceSub: {launches, plural, one {# launch} other {# launches}} · core {core} · catalog {catalog}
performance.card.guidanceTip: What Hive gave each session at launch, on average: its session contract (core), what it adds for the project, the Assistant's role and mode, and its skills' catalog (names and descriptions). Skill bodies are separate: a model reads one only when it uses it.
performance.card.latencyTip: Request time in Hive, from the request to its reply, on a monotonic clock. Percentiles are the bounds of the histogram's buckets.
performance.card.requestsSubRate: {rate, number} an hour recorded · {failed} failed · {cancelled} cancelled
performance.card.requestsTip: Agent API requests (agents’ tools, the Assistant, scripts). An hour: over the time Hive was recording, not the whole range. Failed: refused, client or server errors. Cancelled: the client went away before the reply.
performance.card.toolRepliesSub: {calls, plural, one {characters in # call} other {characters in # calls}} · {size}
performance.card.toolRepliesTip: The text Hive's tools gave the models (what goes into their context), exactly: characters (UTF-16 code units) and UTF-8 bytes. Not tokens.
performance.cards.empty: No card was held in the last {range, select, 24h {24 hours} 7d {7 days} other {30 days}}.
performance.cards.heading: Cards
performance.cards.roundsTip: Review rounds: each failed review is one, and the one under way or passed the next. None before it first went to Review.
performance.cards.tip: Each card its agents held in the last {range, select, 24h {24 hours} 7d {7 days} other {30 days}}: what its builder used while it was in Doing and its reviewer from the review's start to its verdict, as the providers reported it (each card's whole cost, as Provider usage counts whole sessions). ≈ is Hive's estimate; Unknown is what isn't known, never {zero}. Tokens on hover. What a lane's agents used holding no card is its overhead, on the lane's hover in the Progress panel.

performance.compare.measureTip.apiCancel: Requests the client gave up on.
performance.compare.measureTip.apiMs: Time Hive spent on the requests, in all.
performance.compare.measureTip.apiReques: Agent API requests by the session (and agents it started), not the harness’s own.
performance.compare.measureTip.contextBy: What Hive put in the session’s context: launch guidance (core, project, the Assistant’s role and mode, skills’ catalog), the hive tools’ list and every tool reply. Exact UTF-8 bytes, not tokens. Unknown if any part wasn’t measured.
performance.compare.measureTip.costUsd: API-equivalent; only when every sample on both sides has a cost (≈ when Hive estimated one).
performance.compare.measureTip.exportGui: Core, project, the Assistant’s role and mode, and catalog, on average (not per hour).
performance.compare.measureTip.exportReq: Agent API requests, per hour recorded.
performance.compare.measureTip.guidanceB: Core contract, project additions, the Assistant’s role and mode, and the skills’ catalog, at launch.
performance.compare.measureTip.guidanceC: The same parts in characters (UTF-16 code units); the catalog has bytes only.
performance.compare.measureTip.hiveCalls: hive tool calls the server ran (its own log).
performance.compare.measureTip.outputTok: Reasoning included, as the provider reported them.
performance.compare.measureTip.reasoning: Part of output, not added to it.
performance.compare.measureTip.repeatedC: Calls identical to one already made: work done twice.
performance.compare.measureTip.seconds: The scenario’s run, start to end (a model trial’s varies most).
performance.compare.measureTip.skillByte: Delivered skills’ bytes: what was available, not what a model read.
Bytes the skill service read from disk.
performance.compare.measureTip.skillHits: Skills found unchanged (more is fine: shown for the cache scenarios).
performance.compare.measureTip.skillMiss: Skills read again (changed, or not cached).
performance.compare.measureTip.skillScan: The skill service’s scans during the scenario.
performance.compare.measureTip.skillsNot: Skills asked for that the session didn’t get.
performance.compare.measureTip.toolBytes: UTF-8 bytes of the same replies.
performance.compare.measureTip.toolCalls: hive tool calls measured by the bridge.
performance.compare.measureTip.toolChars: Characters of the hive tools’ replies, as the model got them.
performance.compare.measureTip.toolDetai: Calls that asked for the full form.
performance.compare.measureTip.toolError: Tool replies that were errors (the bridge’s count).
performance.compare.measureTip.toolListB: The hive tools’ names, descriptions and schemas as the CLI got them.
performance.compare.notComparable: Not comparable: {reasons} The numbers are shown, but a difference doesn’t mean a change.
performance.compare.note.estimates: Some costs are Hive’s estimates (≈), not the provider’s.
performance.compare.note.fakeUsage: Provider usage isn’t compared: a fake’s tokens are simulated, not a provider’s.
performance.compare.note.leftOut: {n, plural, one {# sample} other {# samples}} left out: {why}.
performance.compare.note.measuredPartly: {n, plural, one {# sample} other {# samples}} measured partly (recording off, measurements dropped or missing): sizes aren’t judged.
performance.compare.note.notJudged: Not judged: some of what it’s judged by wasn’t measured.
performance.compare.note.oneSample: One sample on a side: no spread to judge a change by.
performance.compare.note.partial: {side, select, baseline {The baseline} other {The run}} is partial: {what}.
performance.compare.note.rangesDiffer: The ranges differ in length: compared per hour recorded.
performance.compare.note.realUse: Real use isn’t a controlled workload: a change here can be the work that was done, not Hive.
performance.compare.note.resumed: A resumed session’s provider usage is its whole conversation’s: left out.
performance.compare.note.sameGuidance: Both ran the same guidance revision: differences are in the tools, the API, the skills or the run itself.
performance.compare.note.skillRevisions: The sessions were given different skill revisions.
performance.compare.note.skillRevisionsO: The sessions were given different skill revisions ({names}).
performance.compare.note.stale: {n, plural, one {# sample} other {# samples}} left out: the session was given other guidance than the run started with (stale).
performance.compare.note.usageNotEvery: Provider usage isn’t compared: not every sample reported it.
performance.compare.note.withinSpread: Smaller on average, but within the samples’ spread.
performance.compare.oneMore: Keep or import one more to compare.
performance.compare.partial.dropped: {n, plural, one {# measurement dropped} other {# measurements dropped}} (a limit was full)
performance.compare.partial.evicted: history removed for space in the range
performance.compare.partial.invalid: some of its measurements weren’t valid, so {keys} {n, plural, one {is} other {are}} unknown
performance.compare.partial.projectPart: one project’s part of a workspace export
performance.compare.partial.unattributed: some losses couldn’t be attributed to a project
performance.compare.reason.differentFixt: Different scenario versions (fixtures v{base} and v{run}): the scenarios themselves changed.
performance.compare.reason.differentKind: One is a scenario benchmark and the other a Performance export: they measure different things.
performance.compare.reason.fakeVsModel: A fake provider against a model trial: a fake proves routing and sizes, not a model’s behaviour.
performance.compare.reason.notRecording: Hive wasn’t recording in one of the ranges: there is nothing to compare.
performance.compare.reason.sourceChanged: {side, select, baseline {The baseline’s} other {The run’s}} source changed while it ran: its samples may mix two versions.
performance.compare.regressions: Checks that passed or ran less often
performance.compare.sameFile: The baseline and the run are the same file.
performance.compare.sample.countsDiffer: its check counts don’t match its checks
performance.compare.sample.failedNoCheck: it says it failed, but no check did
performance.compare.sample.invalidCheck: a check in it isn’t valid
performance.compare.scopeName: {kind, select, project {project {project}} own {the workspace’s own work} other {the whole workspace}}
performance.compare.sizesHint: Sizes are exact bytes and characters of what Hive gave the sessions; tokens are only what a provider reported. Skills on disk are what was available, not what a model read. A ~ marks a change within the samples’ spread.
performance.compare.status.betterTip: Less Hive context; every check that passed still passes and still runs; no more calls, failures or retries.
performance.compare.status.failingTip: Checks fail in the run (as often as in the baseline).
performance.compare.status.incompleteTip: Not judged: no completed sample on a side, or what it’s judged by wasn’t fully measured.
performance.compare.status.onlyInBaseTip: The run didn’t run this scenario.
performance.compare.status.onlyInRunTip: New in the run: no baseline for it.
performance.compare.status.sameTip: Within 1% of the baseline, with the same correctness.
performance.compare.status.smallerFailin: Less context, but a check passed (or ran) less often: not an improvement.
performance.compare.status.worseTip: More Hive context, more calls, failures or retries, or a check that passed (or ran) less often.
performance.compare.summary: {n, number} {status, select, better {smaller, still correct} same {no change} worse {larger or worse} smallerFailing {smaller but failing} failing {failing} incomplete {incomplete} onlyInBase {only in baseline} other {only in run}}
performance.compare.unknownTip: Some samples didn’t measure it: unknown, not compared.
performance.compare.usageNotCompared: Provider tokens and cost: not compared (a fake’s are simulated; a model trial’s only when every sample on both sides reported them).
performance.compare.usePart.detail: Work of no project (the Assistant, scripts) and other projects’ work are left out. Losses Hive couldn’t attribute to a project are noted.
performance.compare.usePart.message: This is a workspace export. Only {project}’s part of it can be compared on this project’s page.
performance.compare.usePart.title: Use {project}’s part?

performance.coverage.partial: Recorded for {duration} of it ({percent}){sinceShown, select, yes {, since {since}} other {}}{stretches, plural, =0 {} =1 {} other {, in # stretches}}: before that and in the gaps (Hive closed, recording off, a reset) nothing was seen.

performance.guidance.heading: Guidance at launch
performance.guidance.notGivenTip: {notDelivered, number} asked for but not delivered; {unmeasured, number} delivered but couldn't be measured (left out of the sizes, not counted as zero).
performance.guidance.tip: What Hive gave sessions when they started, per launch on average, exactly. Core: Hive's session contract, the same for every session of a role. Project: what Hive adds for the project (the latest handover's pointer). Role and mode: the Assistant's. Catalog: the skills' names and descriptions (what a CLI lists); on disk: the delivered copies' bytes. A model reads a skill's body only when it uses it, which isn't observable.
performance.heading: Performance
performance.intro.project: What Hive’s Agent API, its tools, the guidance it gives sessions cost, next to what the providers reported. Only this project’s work: the Assistant’s, scripts’ and other projects’ aren’t in it.
performance.intro.workspace: What Hive’s Agent API, its tools, the guidance it gives sessions and its skill service cost, next to what the providers reported.
performance.limits.heading: What isn’t measured
performance.limits.window: This page reads through Hive’s window, not the Agent API: refreshing it adds nothing to these numbers.
performance.noWorkspace: Open a workspace to see its performance.
performance.notRecording: Hive isn’t recording performance metrics, so nothing new is added (what was recorded is still shown).
performance.panel.tip: What Hive's Agent API, its tools, the guidance it gives sessions and its skill service cost. Pick what to look at.
performance.provider.label: Provider
performance.provider.note: Launches and the providers’ usage: the only parts recorded per provider.
performance.provider.nothing: Nothing from {provider} in the last {range, select, 24h {24 hours} 7d {7 days} other {30 days}}{filtered, select, yes { for this filter} other {}}.
performance.providersNote.assistant: The Assistant’s sessions are the workspace’s, not a project’s.
performance.providersNote.scripts: Scripts start no sessions, so they have no provider usage.
performance.range.label: Time range
performance.range.name: {range, select, 24h {24 hours} 7d {7 days} other {30 days}}
performance.routes.heading: Agent API
performance.routes.tip: Requests by route (its template, never the path asked for). The hive tools call these too; a tool call and its request are the same work, so don't add them up.
performance.safeguards.heading: Safeguard stops
performance.safeguards.tip: Responses a CLI's safety classifier stopped, in the sessions active in the range (each session's whole count), per agent and the model each was on. Copilot's sessions don't record them, so they aren't counted.
performance.scope.label: Scope
performance.scope.ownTip: Work of no project: the Hive Assistant, scripts with the workspace token, and Hive’s shared work.
performance.scope.projectTip: Only {project}'s work. Its own Performance tab shows the same.
performance.scope.wholeTip: Every project and the workspace’s own work, each counted once.

performance.skills.cacheTip: Hits: a skill unchanged since it was last read. Changed: read again because its files changed.
performance.skills.heading: Skill service
performance.skills.readSub: {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} · {headers} headers · {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}
performance.skills.tip: Hive's own disk and cache work to know its skills (the status, launches, the Skills view). Shared by the whole workspace, so it is in no project's numbers. A saving in guidance isn't the same as a saving here.
performance.skills.tooBigSub: over the limits (64 MB, 2000 files, 12 deep)
performance.skills.unfiltered: all of it: not per role or provider

performance.tools.tip: Each hive tool's replies as the models got them: characters and UTF-8 bytes, exactly. Detail: calls that asked for the full form. Sorted by characters, what costs a context most.

performance.usage.allUnreadable: Provider usage is unknown: the session history couldn’t be read.
performance.usage.contextTip: Last request's context, over {sessions, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}}: average {avg}, largest {max}{hasWindow, select, yes { of a {window} window} other {}}.
performance.usage.heading: Provider usage
performance.usage.partial: The session history of {unreadable, number} of {hosts, plural, one {# place} other {# places}} (projects, the Assistant) couldn’t be read, so these totals are partial.
performance.usage.tip: What the providers reported for the sessions active in the range, by whose sessions they were: each session's whole usage (so a long session counts in full). Reasoning is part of output, shown separately, not added. Context is a snapshot of each session's last request (average and largest), not a sum. Cost is API-equivalent (≈ estimated by Hive where the provider didn't report it); a subscription isn't billed per this. Sessions that reported nothing are unknown, left out of the totals.
